$comment: GO FURTHER — WHAT HAPPENS AFTER DISCOVERY, AND WHY IT IS NOT IN THE
PRIMARY NAVIGATION.
EuropeDoor's subject is the continent: where places are, what they are
for, and how to move between them. Flying, driving, moving, buying a
home, protecting a digital life and selling a company are all real and
none of them is that — putting seven of them in the masthead would turn
a European atlas into a marketplace navigation bar, which is the one
thing the brand lock and the commercial wall both exist to prevent.
So they are a DECLARED SET with a home of their own: a footer column
and, when the mega-navigation lands, a field inside it. They are never
an editorial recommendation, never ranked, never scored, and never
mixed into a page's own links.
EVERY ROW IS A HOST, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THIS A REGISTER RATHER THAN
A LIST OF LINKS. `checks.py` pins the set of external hosts this site
may navigate to: a new outbound host cannot appear anywhere without a
row here or in data/stay.json, and every such link carries
rel="nofollow noopener" and opens in a new tab.
AND THE TRACKING PARAMETERS ARE STRIPPED. The URLs arrived carrying
`utm_source=chatgpt.com`, which is a claim about where a reader came
from that is false for every reader of this site, and a parameter this
product would not ship even if it were true.
A SERVICE WITH NO DESTINATION IS NOT DRAWN. `fly` is declared and has
no partner, so it renders nothing at all — a row that looks like
navigation and leads nowhere is the failure this repository already
records about a chip that filters nothing and an attribute nobody
reads. It is here so the absence is written down rather than forgotten.
disclosure: Separate services, run by the people behind EuropeDoor and by partners. They are not editorial recommendations and nothing here is ranked or paid for a place in the Atlas.

services.label: Fly
services.why: no flight partner is declared. The trigger is a partner with terms somebody has read.
